title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for General Noisy Inverse Problems
layout_note: Two same-sized conceptual panels side by side, both showing the same geometry: a family of nested green arcs labelled M_4 ... M_0 (noisy data manifolds, fading from pale to dark green toward M_0) crossed by a blue diagonal line with a soft blue glow labelled y = A(x) (the measurement subspace). A sampling trajectory descends from M_4 toward the ground truth x* (red dot) where the line meets M_0. Left: purple score steps, magenta gradient steps and red projection arrows jump onto the blue line and end at x_0 off the manifold. Right (the proposed sampler): purple and magenta steps only, staying on the manifolds and ending at x_0 next to x*.
grouping: No frames: the two panels are separated by whitespace and are identical in background so only the trajectory differs. Each has its own one-line legend along its bottom edge keying the arrow colours (purple s_theta*, magenta gradient of ||y - A(x0_hat)||^2, red 'proj' in the left panel only).
shapes_depth: A soft, painted look: manifold arcs are thick translucent green strokes graded from light (M_4) to dark (M_0); the measurement set is a thin blue line inside a wide blurred blue band. Trajectory steps are short coloured arrows with filled heads; the ground truth and the final sample are small red and blue dots with bold math labels. No boxes at all.
proposed_highlight: The proposed method is the right panel, which removes the red projection arrows: its trajectory keeps to the green manifolds and lands on x* , while the left panel's red jumps to the blue line leave the sample off the manifold. The contrast between the two endpoints carries the claim; neither panel is titled.
lesson: Explain a sampler by drawing the same geometry twice, side by side, and letting only the trajectory change: colour each kind of update step (score, data-gradient, projection) and key it in a one-line legend under each panel, so the missing step type in the proposed panel is the visible difference.

arrangement.units: Two unframed panels of identical size and background, side by side; the left shows a projection-based sampler, the right the proposed one.
arrangement.inputs_as: the measurement as a blue line with a blurred band labelled y = A(x) in bold math, and noise levels as labelled green arcs M_4 ... M_0
arrangement.losses_at: none as boxes; the data-consistency gradient is a magenta step arrow drawn at each point of the trajectory and keyed in the bottom legend
arrangement.shared: the manifolds, measurement line and ground truth x* are redrawn identically in both panels

taxonomy.task: solving noisy (non)linear inverse problems with a pretrained diffusion prior
taxonomy.note: architecture other: posterior sampling that adds a measurement-gradient step to each reverse-diffusion step of a pretrained score model; the figure draws sampling trajectories on data manifolds, not a network. depicts plots: a conceptual geometric diagram of manifolds and a measurement line.

insights.structure: Two identical geometric scenes sit side by side, nested green arcs M_4 to M_0 crossed by a blurred blue measurement line, and only the sampling trajectory drawn over them differs between left and right.
insights.data: Noise levels are drawn as nested arcs that darken toward the clean manifold M_0, the measurement constraint as a thin blue line in a soft glow, and the ground truth and final sample as small red and blue dots labelled x* and x_0.
insights.emphasis: The baseline's red projection arrows jump off the arcs onto the blue line and its x_0 lands away from x*, while the proposed right panel uses only purple and magenta steps and lands on x*, so the absence of red is the contribution.
insights.flow: Each trajectory starts at the top on M_4 and zigzags downward through the arcs, alternating purple score steps with short magenta gradient steps, ending where the blue line meets M_0.
insights.avoid: The two panels carry no titles naming the methods compared, so the reader must find the baseline/proposed split in the caption; the magenta and purple arrows are also very short and close in hue.

notes: Venue from the first page: 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023'. The paper's only architecture-like figure is absent: Fig. 2 is a tiny wrapped probabilistic graph (x0, xt, y) inside the text that `refs crop` could not find ('no caption Figure 2 found'), and Fig. 1 is a results teaser. Fig. 3 is the conceptual method figure (geometry of the sampling path) and is the one carded; it is not a block diagram, so it teaches how to draw an algorithm's mechanism as geometry. Paradigm Score-SDE (the score-based reverse diffusion it guides); DDPM would also fit. Measured on crops/2209.14687/fig3-drawn.png, a copy of fig3.png with no images_px record: the two panels are embedded rasters of drawn artwork (not photos), and with the record `kb measure` masked everything out (photo_share 1.0, empty palette); photo_share is therefore null.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
